title: Time-windowed guarantee allocator and burst reconciliation
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Introduce a time-windowed throughput allocator that enforces contractual guarantees while smoothly reconciling burst credits; adds telemetry for reservation utilization percentiles and a migration guide for Dedicated customers.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated customers have observed oscillations when long-lived traffic patterns interact with burst credits: short sharp bursts are consumed correctly, but long tails cause over-allocation followed by aggressive decommit that violates throughput agreements and spikes latency. This PR introduces a time-windowed guarantee allocator that enforces contractual throughput over configurable windows and a burst reconciliation controller that decays burst credits with hysteresis to avoid ping-pong decommits.

Summary of changes: commits: - introduce windowed throughput allocator algorithm and integration (allocator/windowed_allocator.go) - implement burst-credit reconciler with hysteresis and decay curve (controllers/burst_reconciler.go) - add telemetry exporter for reservation utilization (pkg/telemetry/reservation_reporter.go) - configuration: new throughput contract schema and knobs (config/throughput_contracts.yaml) - unit + integration tests (alloc_test.go, burst_reconciler_integration_test.go) - docs: operations guide and migration notes (docs/dedicated/throughput-windows.md)

What it does: - Enforces contractual throughput guarantees by computing a moving budget over a configurable sliding window (default 5m) rather than a single instantary rate. Requests are admitted against the window budget to preserve long-term guarantees while allowing short bursts. - Keeps a separate burst-credit ledger per-tenant that decays via a two-stage hysteresis function: soft decay (exponential smoothing) and hard decay (linear floor) to prevent immediate credit evaporation when utilization drops. - Reconciliation loop checks for outstanding 'commitment debt' and applies proportional backpressure when headroom is insufficient, with a prioritized fallback to compatible model variants. - Emits telemetry: p50/p90/p99 for reservation utilization, windowed commit fulfillment ratio, credit inflow/outflow counters, and reconciliation events for alerting.

Files changed (high level): - allocator/windowed_allocator.go: core algorithm, admission checks, unit tests. - controllers/burst_reconciler.go: reconciliation loop, hysteresis implementation, mocks for testing. - pkg/telemetry/reservation_reporter.go: aggregator that computes percentile sketches and exposes Prometheus metrics and a compact JSON line for the backend. - config/throughput_contracts.yaml: new schema (window_size, smoothing_factor, min_credit_floor, priority_weights). - e2e/canary/reservation_simulator.go: synthetic workload generator used by integration tests to validate stability under bursty long-tail traffic. - docs/dedicated/throughput-windows.md: operator guide and recommended defaults for migration. - helm/values-dedicated.yaml: adds knobs for window_size and telemetry sampling rate.

Testing summary: - Unit tests cover admission logic, window budget roll-up, and hysteresis math. - Integration canary (local) simulates 100 tenants across three pools; validated that long-tail traffic no longer causes >20% oscillation in reservation utilization across 10 windows. - Load test in benchmark-lab shows median latency improvement during reconcilation windows (p50 down 12ms) and reduction in tail oscillation events. CI: all jobs passed (lint, unit, integration-canary, benchmark-smoke).

Review conversation (high level): - Priya: requested clearer separation between 'window budget' and 'instant quota' to avoid double-counting; author updated allocator to hold separate counters and added explicit comment blocks. - Diego: asked for telemetry cardinality controls; added sampling with configurable rate and an aggregated sketch for high-cardinality tenants. - Liam: flagged potential race in credit decay; added mutex and a small benchmark showing <1% overhead at 10k req/s per pool. - Security review: no customer data surfaced in telemetry, metrics are aggregated; noted in docs.

Migration & rollout plan: - Default behavior behind a feature flag (config: enable_windowed_alloc = false). - Stage rollout: dev -> canary -> production with 10% traffic for 24h, check telemetry: window fulfillment ratio, credit drift, and latency SLOs. - Recommended default knobs: window_size=5m, smoothing_factor=0.12, min_credit_floor=5%. Operators can tune per-tenant via Dedicated Console.

Observability & Alerts added: - alert: WindowedCommitFulfillment < 90% for 3 windows -> Investigate undersupply or misconfiguration. - alert: BurstCreditRunrate > 200% sustained -> Possible misuse or runaway jobs. - dashboard: dedicated/reservations/windowed-overview showing utilization percentiles and credit balances.

Backward compatibility: - New config fields are additive; the prior instant-rate allocator is still available and remains the default until feature flag flip. No breaking API or on-disk format changes.

Risk and mitigations: - Risk: misconfigured window_size could delay reaction to genuine capacity shortfalls. Mitigation: conservative defaults and canary rollout. - Risk: added telemetry may increase cardinality/ingestion. Mitigation: sampling knobs and sketch-based aggregation.

Merge: Squash-merged on 2025-09-18 after two approving reviews. Release note: see release_notes field.

Related: references ENG-1729 (throughput budgeting RFC), SUP-3421 (customer support case describing oscillation), and internal benchmarking doc link: https://redwood-internal/benchmarks/window-allocator-2025-09 (internal).
